normalized_claims.Proposition_30_1: For all natural m>=1 on real l2(N), with positive printed coordinate n=j+1 and alpha=1/m^2, a_n=m^2/(m^2+n^2) is the unique global minimizer of ||Tx-w||^2+alpha||x||^2. Its residual is v_n=n/(m^2+n^2). A=||a||^2 and B=||v||^2 are the full infinite sums; m/4<=A<=4m/3 and 1/[4(m+1)]<=B<=2/m. For all natural K>=m, prefixes contain exactly n=1,...,K, and 0<=A-A_K<=m^4/(3K^3), 0<=B-B_K<=1/K.
normalized_claims.Corollary_30_3: For b_n=1/n^2 and its unique minimum-norm preimage w_n=1/n, c_n=m^2/[n(m^2+n^2)] is the regularized correction at alpha=1/m^2 and ||c-w||^2=B. For every s in the full l2 with ||s-b||<=delta, 0<delta<=1, and literal m=ceil(delta^(-2/3)), ||correction(T,alpha,s)-w||<=sqrt(2/m)+delta*m/2<=(sqrt(2)+1)delta^(1/3).

critical_independent_derivations.claim: Normal equation identifies a global, unique minimizer
critical_independent_derivations.derivation: For n=j+1>0, (n^(-2)+m^(-2))*m^2/(m^2+n^2)=n^(-2). This is (T*T+alpha I)a=T*w in H, not merely coordinates outside H. For any competitor x, expansion gives J(x)-J(a)=||T(x-a)||^2+alpha||x-a||^2. Both terms are nonnegative, and alpha>0 forces x=a at equality.

critical_independent_derivations.claim: Infinite tails have the claimed orientation and constants
critical_independent_derivations.derivation: For x>0, 1/x-1/(x+1)-1/(x+1)^2=1/[x(x+1)^2]>=0; 1/x^2-(1/x-1/(x+1))=1/[x^2(x+1)]>=0; and 1/(3x^3)-1/(3(x+1)^3)-1/(x+1)^4=(6x^2+4x+1)/[3x^3(x+1)^4]>=0. Finite telescoping at x=K+j gives the upper bounds 1/K and 1/(3K^3). The lower square comparison starts at x=K+1, giving 1/(K+1) after the reciprocal remainder tends to zero. Summability is established before identifying norms and tails.

critical_independent_derivations.claim: All four bounds follow without a truncation surrogate
critical_independent_derivations.derivation: For n<=m, a_n>=1/2, yielding A>=m/4. With a_n^2<=1 on the prefix and <=m^4/n^4 outside it, A<=4m/3. The elementary inequality mn<=m^2+n^2 gives v_n^2<=1/m^2, so the prefix contributes <=1/m; the tail contributes <=1/m. For n>m, v_n>=1/(2n), and the lower reciprocal-square tail gives B>=1/[4(m+1)].

critical_independent_derivations.claim: Actual attainable datum and bias, not an assumed generic model
critical_independent_derivations.derivation: T w=b coordinatewise. All weights 1/(j+1) are nonzero, so the preimage is unique. T commutes with its normal operator because T*=T and alpha is scalar; applying T to the a-normal equation gives the c-normal equation for c=T a and b=T w. Thus c is the universal correction for b. Algebra gives w-c=v, and the norm square is B.

critical_independent_derivations.claim: Sharp deterministic noise amplification and literal rounding
critical_independent_derivations.derivation: For e=correction(s)-correction(b), the normal equation gives ||Te||^2+alpha||e||^2=<s-b,Te><=delta||Te||. Completing the square yields 4alpha||e||^2<=delta^2. With sqrt(alpha)=1/m this is ||e||<=delta*m/2. The triangle inequality adds bias <=sqrt(2/m). Put u=delta^(-2/3)>=1 and m=ceil(u), then u<=m<=2u. Because u*(delta^(1/3))^2=1 and delta*u=delta^(1/3), the two terms sum to at most (sqrt(2)+1)delta^(1/3).
